bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: UAE geopolitical instability impacting real estate demand or supply chains; slower-than-expected capacity utilization ramp-up in India (Glasstech units); raw material price volatility if pass-through mechanisms fail; execution risk on new product launches.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly optimistic and confident despite external headwinds; emphasizes 'genie in the bottle' regarding UAE resilience; transparent about integration teething issues in India; bullish on FY27 margin expansion to 18%.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: India revenue degrowth on a proforma basis (including pre-acquisition Glasstech) due to 2-quarter consolidation/re-engineering period and cessation of low-margin trading activities. Zero tax liability expected for next 2 years enhances cash flow. Saint-Gobain collaboration provides 4-5% price advantage and preferential order confirmation, not just marketing support.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Access to European-standard glass processing technologies
- Exclusive, royalty-free technology licensing agreement with Polymer Technology SRO (Spain) for fire-rated glass, seen as uncommon among domestic manufacturers
- Multi-location manufacturing platform across India (Silvassa, Taloja, Erode) and UAE (Ras Al-Khaimah) providing geographic diversification and load-balancing/cross-utilisation of management resources
- Established UAE subsidiary with strong market positioning across the GCC construction sector
- Centralised procurement practices to manage raw-material cost fluctuations
- Automation-led manufacturing with real-time production monitoring, quality analytics and predictive/preventive maintenance
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and global economic risk — Geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and volatility in global economic conditions may impact infrastructure investments, construction activity and export demand across key markets, particularly in GCC countries; fluctuations in energy prices and logistics costs may also affect operational stability and project execution timelines.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Changes in government regulations, taxation policies, environmental norms, labour laws and trade-related regulations across domestic and international markets may affect operational efficiency and compliance requirements within the flat glass industry.
- Raw material and energy cost risk — Manufacturing operations remain exposed to fluctuations in prices and availability of key raw materials such as glass, interlayers, chemicals and related inputs; variability in fuel, power and logistics costs may also impact operating margins and overall cost competitiveness.
- Competitive market risk — The value-added glass industry remains highly competitive with the presence of organised and regional players across architectural and processed glass segments; increasing competition and pricing pressure may impact market share and profitability.
- Information technology and cybersecurity risk — Dependence on information technology systems across manufacturing, supply chain, finance and business operations exposes the Company to risks from system disruptions, cyber threats, data breaches and operational downtime.
- Financial and liquidity risk — The Company remains exposed to risks related to liquidity management, interest rate fluctuations, working capital requirements and changes in overall market conditions, which may impact financial performance and cash flows.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: UAE: Dominant revenue contributor (~60% of FY26), focused on high-margin IG and Laminated glass for facades. India: Transitioning from plain tempered (low margin) to IG/Laminated. business.body: Sejal Glass Limited, founded in 1998, is an architectural glass processing company manufacturing toughened glass, laminated glass, insulated glass units and decorative/specialised glass solutions for residential and commercial buildings, public infrastructure, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, industrial facilities, data centres and high-security applications. It operates manufacturing facilities in Silvassa, Taloja and Erode (India) and Ras Al-Khaimah (UAE), serving both domestic and international markets including the GCC region; overall tempering capacity increased during FY2025-26 to 24.01 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum from 7.80 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum following the acquisition of Glasstech Industries' architectural glass manufacturing business.

latest_quarter.body: Raw material (float glass) prices up 7-8% due to energy surcharges; company passing through 80-90% of cost increases. Consolidated gross margin ~33-34% (UAE mix superior to India). India gross margin expansion expected as mix shifts from 60% plain tempered to high-value IG/Laminated, potentially lifting gross margin to 39-40% long-term.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 25% base case (up to 40% if UAE stabilizes) for FY27; Target Topline >INR 500cr. Margin: 17.5%-18% EBITDA for FY27. Order Inflow: UAE maintaining AED 10.2-10.5mn/month; India Q1 FY27 expecting 20% QoQ growth. Capex/Commissioning: UAE expansion machines delayed by geopolitics, now scheduled for installation in Q2/Q3 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Strong visibility in UAE with AED 60mn (~INR 135-140cr) order book; Q1 FY27 revenue visibility of AED 31mn, improving to AED 35mn in Q2. India order book growing via railway tenders (Vande Bharat) and commercial projects.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New product lines (Fire-rated from Spain, Bullet-proof, Digital printed) launching Q3 FY26, targeting 5-7% revenue mix in FY26 and 15-20% in FY27. Railway segment entry (2-3% revenue contribution). Geographic diversification: Exports to Europe initiated from India; African market push from UAE.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen position in value-added and speciality glass segments
- Improve capacity utilisation across facilities, particularly the newly acquired Taloja and Erode units
- Expand presence in both domestic and international markets to reduce geographic concentration risk and create a more balanced business
- Continue investing in technology and automation (advanced manufacturing equipment, automation-led systems, intelligent monitoring)
- Diversify product portfolio into specialised, high-value segments — fire-rated glass, railway-grade glass, bullet-resistant glass and digitally printed glass
- Use centralised procurement practices to manage raw-material cost fluctuation
- Pursue R&D focused on product innovation, process improvement, systems integration and sustainability
- Build a unified organisational culture and leadership pipeline across manufacturing locations and international operations ("One Sejal" philosophy; Lakshya 2030 vision-alignment programme)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY2025-26 Sejal Glass acquired and operationalised two manufacturing units of Glasstech Industries (India) Pvt Ltd at Taloja (Maharashtra) and Erode (Tamil Nadu), transforming the Company from a single-location to a multi-location manufacturing platform and taking overall tempering capacity from 7.80 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum to 24.01 lakh sq. mtrs. per annum. The Taloja facility's modern furnace, equipped with Fully Conventional Technology, opened up a new Digital Printing Glass segment and also strengthened capabilities in bullet-resistant glass and advanced façade solutions; as a recently integrated facility it is described as carrying substantial capacity headroom for future growth. The Silvassa facility remains the core domestic manufacturing pillar (toughened, laminated, insulated and decorative glass). Cross-facility capacity utilisation across the manufacturing ecosystem is described as reflecting a mix of mature facilities running at healthy utilisation and newly integrated facilities (Taloja) providing strategic headroom; the UAE subsidiary's own capacity utilisation improved to 67% in FY2025-26 from 53% in FY2024-25. Going forward, the Company intends to expand domestically via geographic expansion and infrastructure-led opportunities, leverage its UAE platform for the GCC, Africa and other export markets, and continue to evaluate disciplined inorganic growth along with selective brownfield and greenfield expansion aligned with market demand, technology access and return expectations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Residential and commercial real estate momentum, particularly premium housing, office spaces and data centres, continues to support demand
- Investments across airports, metro rail, healthcare and hospitality projects creating opportunities for architectural glass solutions
- Government focus on rail modernisation, including high-speed train programmes and rolling stock upgrades, creating growing demand for specialised glazing solutions
- Growing focus on energy efficiency and sustainable construction, reinforced by green building standards and energy performance codes, accelerating adoption of insulated and laminated glass solutions
- UAE/GCC construction activity supporting international operations, though geopolitical developments caused volatility in regional trade flows and some near-term supply-chain disruption
- Improved capacity utilisation at the UAE subsidiary (rising to 67% in FY2025-26 from 53% in FY2024-25) driving consolidated revenue and margin improvement
- Standalone EBITDA margin moderated due to under-utilisation of capacity at the newly acquired Taloja/Erode units, which were operational for only part of the year
- Newer product categories (fire-rated glass, railway-grade glass, bullet-resistant glass) expected to contribute more as recently integrated facilities ramp up utilisation
- Industry-wide competitive intensity from organised and unorganised players, raw-material cost volatility, and dependence on construction/real-estate cycles remain structural demand risks
- UAE operations remained steady through the year, supported by a healthy order book and strong payment discipline across the customer base

deepdive.thesis: Sejal Glass delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with 72% YoY revenue growth and 17.5% EBITDA margins, driven by UAE resilience and initial Glasstech integration. The core investment story pivots to FY27 where India operations (currently low utilization) must ramp to 50%+ to unlock consolidated 18% margin guidance, offsetting potential UAE volatility.

open.item: Company expects increasing contributions from newer product categories (fire-rated glass, railway-grade glass, bullet-resistant glass), with recently integrated facilities playing a larger role as utilisation improves.
Management expects higher utilisation of the newly acquired Taloja and Erode capacities, together with continued cost optimisation, to deliver sustainable growth and improved margins.

Management expects that higher utilisation of the acquired capacities, continued operational efficiencies and cost optimisation, together with sustained UAE subsidiary performance, will deliver sustainable growth and improved margins.

Proceeds from the FY2025-26 preferential issue are intended to be used for working capital requirements, repayment of debts, capital expenditure (development/refurbishment/renovation of assets), business opportunities, strategic initiatives and/or investment in subsidiaries; no deviation in utilisation reported so far.

Taloja, as a recently integrated facility, is described as providing substantial capacity headroom to support future growth and to enhance flexibility and scalability of the overall manufacturing network.

Company intends to strengthen its domestic presence through geographic expansion and infrastructure-led opportunities, leverage its UAE platform for the GCC, Africa and export markets, and continue to evaluate disciplined inorganic growth along with selective brownfield and greenfield expansion aligned with market demand, technology access and return expectations.
